title: September 25 Project Connect - Avondale
description:
### Event Description  
**Project Connect** is a one-stop resource event led by Keys to Change and designed to assist individuals who are experiencing or at risk of experiencing homelessness.  

This event brings together a wide range of service providers offering on-the-spot support, including:

- Housing or shelter access  
- Medicaid and nutrition assistance  
- Clothing and meals  
- Substance use treatment  
- Employment readiness services  
- Social Security assistance  
- Mental health support  
- And much more  

### Why Volunteers Are Needed  
Volunteers play a critical role in helping the event run smoothly and ensuring that guests feel welcomed, supported, and able to access the services they need.

### What You'll Be Doing  
By signing up, volunteers may assist with:

- Guest navigation and check-in  
- Distributing meals or supplies  
- Supporting service providers  
- Helping with event setup or teardown  
- Creating a warm, respectful environment for all attendees  

Your time and care can make a real difference in someone's life—thank you for showing up and serving our community!
accessibility_notes: Volunteers may be asked to work both indoors and outdoors in high temperatures (potentially exceeding 100°F). Air-conditioned breaks and rest opportunities will be provided throughout the day at your leisure. Please bring water and a snack and hydrate well the day and night prior. If you have any accessibility needs or require accommodations, please contact us in advance—we are happy to support and accommodate you.

title: Estate Planning 101 With Attorney Jacquelyne J. Mingle
description:
Most people know that having a will is important. Still, many don’t have one. But get this: Having just a will is often not enough. Without crucial documents, people are leaving themselves and their estates vulnerable. Join Sky Island Alliance and Tucson attorney Jacquelyne J. Mingle to learn estate planning basics and a bit more. This free public event is brought to you by [Sky Island Alliance](https://skyislandalliance.org/), [Planned Giving Roundtable of Southern Arizona](https://www.pgrtsa.org/), and [Mission Management & Trust Co](https://missiontrust.com/). 

**About Our Speaker**

Jacquelyne J. Mingle has been practicing in Tucson for more than a decade, and her practice encompasses a variety of elder law issues, including estate planning; estate and trust administration; and disputes over wills, trusts, and estates. She is a fellow of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel, is one of U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Lawyers,” and is certified by the State Bar of Arizona as a Specialist in Estate and Trust Law. She is licensed as a fiduciary by the Arizona Supreme Court and served as chair of the State Bar’s Elder Law, Mental Health and Special Needs Planning Council and served on the Estate & Trust Law Advisory Commission for the State Bar’s Board of Legal Specialization. She also serves on the board of directors for the Southern Arizona Estate Planning Council and Tohono Chul Park. Jacque’s J.D. is from the U of A’s James E. Rogers College of Law, where she has taught the Trusts & Estates course as an adjunct professor. Before becoming an attorney, Jacque was an editor at USA Today supervising entertainment coverage. She did her undergraduate work at the University of Kansas and roots for both the Jayhawks (Rock Chalk!) and the Wildcats (Bear Down!).

title: Swing Left WA - Book Club: On Tyranny by Timothy Snyder
description:
If you haven't heard of it, On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons from the Twentieth Century is a book published in 2017 by Timothy Snyder, a historian of 20th-century Europe. Rachel Maddow has frequently invited him back on her show to explain how we can make sense of the current moment. ([Here is one appearance earlier this year](https://youtu.be/nNrbInmlHhA?si=zTCn8t-kXWaP5tJ9)). This book is more relevant than ever. Many of the warnings in the book are unfolding before our eyes right now. So, it's crucial to know how to recognize these signs, and more importantly, what we can learn from history and do differently this time.

The book is fairly short, only 126 pages, and would take just 2-3 hours to finish. If you need to purchase a copy, consider buying from a local bookstore.

title: Knock Doors for Daniel Hernandez in Avondale!
description:
Canvass for Daniel Hernandez in Avondale!   Come join us to knock doors and talk to voters about the upcoming primary election!

About Daniel: As the first in his family to go to college, Daniel attended the University of Arizona where he interned for then-Congresswoman Gabby Giffords. Daniel was a survivor of the 2011 Tucson shooting and was the first to administer first aid before EMTs arrived on the scene. Turning tragedy into resilience, Daniel decided to live a life of public service to protect Arizonan families and served on the Sunnyside School board (2011-2015) and was later elected to the Arizona State Legislature (2017-2022). Now, Daniel is running for Congress to Fight the Trump Administration to protect Arizonans' social security and healthcare access, expand federal dollars into public education, and lower the cost of everyday goods and housing.

description:
**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**
NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.


🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨


The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.


**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**
Check out nokings.org for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*
